entities.summary:
Bank of America Corporation is an American multinational investment bank and financial services holding company founded in San Francisco in 1904 as the Bank of Italy by Amadeo Giannini. Renamed Bank of America in 1930, it became the world's largest bank by assets during the mid-20th century and remains one of the largest financial institutions globally.

Giannini's founding innovation was extending credit to working-class immigrants and small businesses when other banks served only the wealthy, pioneering branch banking across California. Bank of America also created the first general-purpose credit card, BankAmericard (now Visa), in 1958, which transformed consumer credit globally. The bank financed much of California's postwar suburban expansion and agricultural industry.

After multiple mergers including FleetBoston (2004) and Merrill Lynch (2008), Bank of America became a universal bank combining retail, investment, and wealth management services. The 2008 Merrill Lynch acquisition during the financial crisis was controversial but made BofA a Wall Street giant. With $3+ trillion in assets and 66 million customers, it remains one of the 'Big Four' US banks shaping global capital flows.
